summary: This case study details a practical implementation of an append-only credit ledger on Cloudflare D1 (SQLite) where traditional PostgreSQL-style row locks like SELECT FOR UPDATE are unavailable. It provides a clear architectural breakdown, examining balance computation via SUM queries, unique constraint idempotency handling, and concurrency trade-offs.
strengths: Addresses a concrete, highly relevant architectural challenge for building serverless billing systems on SQLite/Cloudflare D1.
Provides realistic code snippets and contrasts documented architectural intentions with actual schema/code reality.
Clearly documents concurrency limits, failure modes, and race condition considerations regarding different versus same idempotency keys.
weaknesses: Relies on code descriptions without a publicly accessible repository, relying entirely on text-based inspection.
Lacks production load-testing verification, relying on local Miniflare tests instead.
suggestions: Provide a public template repository demonstrating the D1 schema and Vitest suite for hands-on reproduction.
Expand on mitigation strategies for the acknowledged different-key concurrency over-spend race condition.

claims.text: Cloudflare D1 is SQLite. The Worker API is prepare, batch, exec, and sessions for sequential consistency.
SQLite does not implement SELECT FOR UPDATE.
Miniflare is an open-source simulator for Cloudflare Workers that uses in-memory SQLite for D1 databases.

novelty_vs_existing.title: HMAC-SHA256 Stripe Dispute Webhooks on Cloudflare Workers Without stripe-node
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Focuses specifically on the credit ledger balance computation and race conditions on Cloudflare D1 rather than Stripe webhook verification.
